facts.statement: The genus Normanniasaurus was first described and named by Jean Le Loeuff, Suravech Suteethorn, and Eric Buffetaut in 2013.
facts.quote: Normanniasaurus was first described and named by Jean Le Loeuff, Suravech Suteethorn and Eric Buffetaut in 2013

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Normanniasaurus genceyi.
facts.quote: the type species is Normanniasaurus genceyi

facts.statement: The specific name genceyi honors Pierre Gencey, who discovered the remains in July 1990.
facts.quote: The specific name, genceyi, honors Mr. Pierre Gencey who discovered the remains in July 1990.

facts.statement: The holotype specimens of Normanniasaurus are housed at the Museum d'histoire naturelle du Havre.
facts.quote: Normanniasaurus is known from the holotype MHNH-2013.2.1.1 through MHNH-2013.2.1.12 housed at the Museum d'histoire naturelle du Havre

facts.statement: The known fossil material includes a partial skeleton with presacral vertebrae fragments, a partial sacrum, anterior and middle caudal vertebrae, a right scapula, ilia and ischia fragments, and parts of the femur and fibula.
facts.quote: A partial skeleton including presacral vertebrae fragments, a partial sacrum, an anterior and a middle caudal vertebrae, a right scapula, fragments of both ilia and ischia, the proximal end of a femur and the proximal part of a fibula.

facts.statement: Normanniasaurus lived during the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately 113 to 107 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 113 a 107 millones de años, durante el Albiense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Normanniasaurus is classified as a basal titanosaurian.
Normanniasaurus genceyi is the only known species of the extinct genus Normanniasaurus, a saurópodo titanosaurian dinosaur.
facts.quote: Normanniasaurus genceyi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Normanniasaurus de dinosaurio saurópodo, titanosauriano

facts.statement: Normanniasaurus shares several primitive characteristics with slightly younger basal titanosaurians such as Epachthosaurus and Andesaurus.
facts.quote: Comparte varias características primitivas con titanosaurios basales ligeramente más jóvenes, como Epachthosaurus y Andesaurus.

facts.statement: The late Early Cretaceous radiation of basal Titanosauria in South America, Europe, and Africa is considered unusual.
facts.quote: La radiación tardía del Cretácico temprano de Titanosauria basal en América del Sur, Europa y África es inusual.

facts.statement: The time range for Normanniasaurus is the Albian stage, from 110.1 to 106.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (110.1 to 106.3 million years ago)
